## Purpose and Runtime Topology
Ghidra MCP exposes Ghidra reverse-engineering operations as an MCP tool catalog. An AI/MCP client talks to a Python bridge; the bridge routes calls to a Ghidra-resident Java HTTP service, which operates on Ghidra programs and projects. The Java service runs either as a CodeBrowser plugin or standalone headless process.
- `python/bridge_mcp_ghidra/__main__.py`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/GhidraMCPPlugin.java`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/headless/GhidraMCPHeadlessServer.java`

## Client-facing MCP Bridge
The Python package is the primary client entry point (`bridge-mcp-ghidra`). It provides stdio, streamable HTTP, and deprecated SSE MCP transports; discovers/selects Ghidra instances; registers tool groups lazily or eagerly; validates schemas; and dispatches dynamic tools to the Java HTTP API. Static bridge tools remain available before a Ghidra connection.
- `python/bridge_mcp_ghidra/cli.py`
- `python/bridge_mcp_ghidra/server.py`
- `python/bridge_mcp_ghidra/dispatch.py`

## Java Server Lifecycle and Transport Boundary
The plugin/headless runtimes share server lifecycle, endpoint definitions, request/response serialization, authentication, and transports. TCP/HTTP supports normal local operation; Unix-domain-socket support enables instance discovery/local routing. The GUI runtime must marshal Ghidra API work onto Swing threads, while headless executes directly.
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/ServerManager.java`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/TcpTransport.java`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/UdsHttpServer.java`

## Endpoint Catalog and Service Layer
Endpoint registration maps validated parameters to domain services. The core layer is organized around Ghidra program state: functions, listings/comments, data types, analysis, symbols, xrefs/call graphs, scripts, emulation, and malware analysis. Services are the boundary between HTTP/MCP contracts and Ghidra APIs, and include convention/naming enforcement and batch/atomic write behavior.
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/EndpointDef.java`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/FunctionService.java`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/DataTypeService.java`

## Program Context and Execution Modes
`ProgramProvider` abstracts how a request resolves its target program. GUI providers use the active CodeBrowser/front-end context; multi-tool support handles multiple open programs; headless providers own program/project loading independently. This is a material safety boundary because omitted selectors can fall back to a shared current program unless the bridge’s strict selector mode is enabled.
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/ProgramProvider.java`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/MultiToolProgramProvider.java`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/headless/HeadlessProgramProvider.java`

## Headless, Project, and Deployment Paths
Headless mode supports binary loading, auto-analysis, project lifecycle, Ghidra archive/zip import-export, and shared Ghidra Server version-control operations without a GUI. Docker packages this server for automation. The supported developer entry point is the Python setup CLI, which installs Ghidra dependencies, builds the Java extension through Maven, and deploys it into a Ghidra profile.
- `docker/Dockerfile`
- `tools/setup/cli.py`
- `pom.xml`

## External Systems and Security
Material dependencies are Java 21, Ghidra 12.1.x APIs, Python 3.10+, Maven, and optional Docker. Ghidra Server is an external shared-project/version-control service. An optional external debugger service is reached by the Python bridge via `GHIDRA_DEBUGGER_URL`. Non-loopback Java-server binds require bearer authentication; script execution and filesystem access are separately gated.
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/SecurityConfig.java`
- `src/main/java/com/xebyte/core/GhidraMCPAuthenticator.java`
- `python/bridge_mcp_ghidra/debugger.py`
